data.text:
**Claim 0: primary settling removes about 60% of solids, about a third of the dissolved waste**
- AIChE glossary, primary wastewater treatment: 'Primary treatment plants generally remove 25 to 35 percent of the Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD) and 45 to 65 percent of the total suspended matter.' URL: https://www.aiche.org/ifs/resources/glossary/isws-water-glossary/primary-wastewater-treatment
- Seoul National University lecture notes: 'Primary treatment: remove ~60% of SS and ~35% of BOD.' URL: https://ocw.snu.ac.kr/sites/default/files/NOTE/11176.pdf
- Verdict: supported in a corrected form: a settling tank removes about 45 to 65 percent of the solids and only 25 to 35 percent of the waste that uses up oxygen.

**Claim 1: 82 gallons a day at home**
- EPA WaterSense statistics and facts: 'each American uses an average of 82 gallons of water a day at home' (USGS 2015). URL: https://19january2025snapshot.epa.gov/watersense/statistics-and-facts
- Verdict: supported as written (82 gallons a day at home; that most goes down the drain is not in the source).

**Claim 2: digesters make biogas, mostly methane**
- Suez water handbook, characteristic anaerobic digestion parameters: CH4 60 to 65% for sludge. URL: https://www.suezwaterhandbook.com/water-and-generalities/fundamental-biological-engineering-processes-applicable-to-water-treatment/anaerobic-bacterial-cultures/characteristic-anaerobic-digestion-parameters
- Riga conference paper (Dubrovskis): 59.0% methane in biogas from fresh sludge. URL: https://iitf.lbtu.lv/conference/proceedings2010/Papers/40_Dubrovskis_Vilis_2_anaerobic.pdf
- Verdict: supported in a corrected form: sludge digester gas is about 60 percent methane.
